markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (47%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Invasive narrowly leads InSitu (40%) [F1], the image is flagged, and no similar case is invasive.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 47%, InSitu 40% | Narrow margin |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.76; 98th percentile | Flagged, atypical image [F6] |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models pick different classes |
| Similar cases | 0/5 invasive; 5/5 InSitu | Neighbors favor InSitu [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 0) · ↑ invasive · Case score above typical · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 0) · ↓ invasive · Scored high; small negative term here · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Typical score; caption check inconsistent [F4] · Weak
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 9) · ↑ invasive · Positive term here, against expected direction; spot check 12/20 · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 3, 5) · ↑ invasive · Scored high; spot check 3/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis (3/20) and mitoses (0/20) are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- The image is out of distribution (98th percentile), so probabilities may not transfer.
- In situ is correct: all 5 similar cases are InSitu and MUSK disagrees.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 1, 3** — highest invasive contribution; look for stromal invasion versus in situ growth.
2. **Region 9** — confirm whether atypical cells stay confined within ducts.
3. **Regions 3, 5** — verify necrosis visually; its AI spot check was poor.
